tlf_ctr_doi <- "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23349388"

doi_to_badge <- function(doi) 
  paste0("[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/", 
                     gsub("https://doi.org/", "", doi, fixed = TRUE),
                     ".svg)](", doi, ")")

tlf_pp_badge  <- doi_to_badge(tlf_pp_doi)
tlf_ctr_badge <- doi_to_badge(tlf_ctr_doi)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The repository contains all code to produce the pre-specified statistical analyses. This includes all analyses and results for the primary publication and pre-specified secondary analyses. 

The primary publication of the DEXA-PSYCH trial was published in [JOURNAL]() and available [here]() (Links will be updated upon publication.)

The DEXA-PSYCH trial has EU Trial registration number [2022-501428-45-00](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en) with WHO universal Trial Identifier U1111-1280-7614.

The Trial protocol is available [here](https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public/view/2022-501428-45-00?lang=en) in its latest version and an earlier version is presented in [Rømer et al (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-025-08989-2)

The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) was archived and locked in a persistent and immutable [Zenodo DOI](`r sap_doi`) prior to unblinding of the randomization list. The time of unblinding coincides with locking of the database and is called *database lock* (DBL).

The code is released in two versions: 
[pre-dbl-v1.0](`r pre_dbl_url`) and [post-dbl-v1.0](`r post_dbl_url`). 
Each version is archived in [Zenodo DOIs](`r code_doi`) and any differences between the two versions of the code base is documented. 

All code was written by Senior Statistician Rune Haubo B Christensen and Statistician and PhD Researcher Eva Nina Sparre Wandall. 


## Table, Listings and Figures books

The code in this repository produces two Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) books; a primary publication version and a clinical trial report (CTR) version. 
All outcomes are reported from day 0 to day 28. Long term follow-up (until 6 months after baseline) will be presented separately.

1. Primary Publication: 
This version documents all summaries and statistical analyses for safety and efficacy endpoints presented in the primary publication as documented in the SAP and trial protocol. This version is archived in a Zenodo DOI [here](`r tlf_pp_doi`).
1. Clinical Trial Protocol (CTR): This version includes all content reported in the primary publication version but also presents results for additional secondary outcomes. Contents for the secondary outcomes will be released upon publication of secondary papers presenting the additional secondary outcomes. This version of the TLF-book is archived in a Zenodo DOI [here](`r tlf_ctr_doi`).

The primary publication TLF-book is available [here](https://dexa-psych.netlify.app/) although it is password-protected for reviewer access until the primary publication is published.


## Description of the code base

All code is written in **R** using [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) to produce browsable TLF-books hosted online.

The code is written such that all analyses can be run by execution of the file: `39_run_all/00_run_all.Rmd` provided there is access to the raw data. The raw trial data in the form of a `.csv` file and an `.r` file are held on a secure drive and are not publicly available due to data privacy restrictions. 

The code is structured around the following key elements:

1. Metadata `.csv`-files that provide structured information on all tables, figures and listings.
1. An automatic analysis pipeline which auto-generates the majority of analyses, tables and figures complete with captions, footnotes and organized in parts, chapters, sections and subsections.
1. Manual analyses in separate scripts supplement the automatic pipeline. Products of the manual analyses are also included in metadata.
1. A library of custom written **R** functions on which both the automatic pipeline, data processing and manual analyses rely.
1. The **R**-package [data.table](https://r-datatable.com/) is used for data handling. The **R**-package [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com/) is used to format all tables. 
1. `.qmd`-files for each chapter of each book are auto-generated from metadata and points to `html`-tables and `.png`-figures generated by the analysis pipeline.

Additionally we write all scripts in the form of **R**-markdown (`.Rmd`) files. This has the advantage that each script can be executed in a fresh R-process providing integrity of the results, and that the resulting `html`-files provide humanly readable results of scripts. The scripts can be executed using the `rmarkdown` package `rmarkdown::("my-rmd-file.Rmd")`, by pressing the `knit` button in the 
[RStudio editor](https://posit.co/products/open-source/rstudio).


### Structure of repository contents

The code is organized in the following folder structure:

- `01_data_input`: Definitions of supplementary variable names.
- `03_checksums`: SHA-256 checksums for the raw data to confirm identity of raw data.
- `10_metadata`: 2 files: 
  - `tlf_registry.csv`: Registry of all tables, listings, and figures produced by the code.
  - `table_footers.csv`: Footnotes for automatic application to tables and figures in the resulting TLF-books.
- `20_functions`: Custom written **R** functions for analyses and processing.
- `30_process_data` : Scripts processing the raw data preparing them for statistical analysis.
- `32_manual_analyses`: Scripts with analyses that supplement the automatic pipeline.
- `34_tlf_pipeline`: Scripts that execute the automatic pipeline generating the majority of results. Additional scripts that build on results produced earlier in the pipeline are also placed here. The final script that runs `quarto` to produce the TLF-books is placed last.
- `39_run_all`: The `00_run_all.Rmd` script that executes all code in the repo.
- `40_tlf_source`: Files required to produce Quarto-books with results. 
- `80_parallel_programming`: In addition to the automatic analysis in the pipeline, the primary analysis of the primary endpoint is also independently programmed by two separate statisticians (RHBC and ENSW). A separate script compares the results of the independently programmed scripts to each other and compares these results to those produced by the pipeline. An error is reported if any differences in results are found.


### Materials produced by the code

Running the code to produce TLF-books with all analyses, tables and figures generates the following materials:

- `04_data_checks`: QC-checks of data.
- `05_cache`: `.csv`-file with simple cache of unconditional exact tests. Computing the confidence interval for the odds-ratio parameter takes a substantial amount of time so to save time on subsequent runs this cache is generated. The cache has no influence on the results; only on the computing time.
- `50_output_db`: data base with information on all statistical results from the automatic pipeline stored as `.rds`-files. MMRM-imputed datasets are also stored here.
- `60_tlf_book_all`: Internal QC-version of the TLF-book.
- `60_tlf_book_ctr`: CTR-version of TLF-book.
- `60_tlf_book_pp`: Primary publication version of TLF-book.


### Computing environment

The repository is equipped with an [`renv.lock`](`r renvlock_url`)-file which makes the **R**-package environment reproducible by capturing all versions and inter-dependencies. To re-create the **R** environment used to produce this book, 
[clone](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/cloning-a-repository?tool=desktop) 
the [repository](`r url`), open [R](https://www.r-project.org/) and run `renv::restore()`. 
For further information see [the renv package homepage](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/).


## How to cite this work 

For citation in published works, please cite the primary publication and any relevant DOI given above---citation information is available in each of them. 
The code base repository also has citation information available in a [CITATION.cff file](`r citation_url`). 


## REDCap data export

Raw data are exported from REDCap as follows:

1. Choose "Data exports, ..." under Applications on the left
1. Choose "Export Data" for export name: "rchr_data"
1. Choose **R** as export format; Leave all options in the middle column un-selected; in the right column choose 
   1. Export gray Form Status fields with blank value
   1. ", (comma) - default"
   1. Use period/full stop (.) as decimal for all numbers
1. Choose "Export Data" (bottom right) and download both **R**-file (`*.r`) and data-file (`*.csv`)

When exporting data from Redcap and choosing **R** two files will be generated:

1. A data `.csv` file containing all raw data.
1. An `.r`-code file with 
  (a) labels for all variables; these are text strings describing the contents of the variable, and 
  (b) levels of categorical variables (called 'factors' in **R**).

- Store both files (which are date and time stamped) under a logged and audited Windows network drive.

Rather than running the **R**-code in the `.r`-file we extract the information on labels and factor levels by computing on the text that is the content of the file.
